bullets.title: Fed hike odds jump to 36% at July 29 meeting; bond yields at multi-year highs
bullets.body: Futures markets are pricing a 36% probability of a rate hike at the July 29 FOMC meeting, a notable jump. Separately, US 30-year bond yields have been above 5% for the longest stretch since 2007, while real yields on 10-year Treasuries hit their highest level since 2023 — a macro headwind for growth and tech stocks. One commentator notes that with higher oil/risk premium pushing up the neutral rate, the Fed staying on hold constitutes de facto easing.

bullets.title: AMD lands $5B Anthropic deal: 2GW MI450 GPU order + $5B equity investment
bullets.body: AMD and Anthropic announced a major strategic partnership: AMD will invest up to $5B in Anthropic, while Anthropic commits to purchasing up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's next-generation Instinct MI450/MI455 chips starting H1 2027. AMD will also use Anthropic's Claude models for internal software development. The deal mirrors NVIDIA's prior Anthropic investment playbook and broadly validates AMD's AI compute capabilities as a credible NVDA alternative.

bullets.title: OpenAI raises 2030 capex forecast to $750B; launches $20B Georgia data center
bullets.body: OpenAI increased its compute spending projection through 2030 to ~$750B, up from ~$600B earlier in the year, and is initiating Project Camellia, a $20B data center near the Georgia coast in Effingham. AI capex is accelerating broadly: Google's capex is on track to nearly triple in two years, and xAI/SpaceX are exploring large-scale Texas data center expansion.

bullets.title: Software sector down ~4% in two days as 'AI Doom' trade resurges
bullets.body: The software sector (IGV) fell another 2.5% on the day and is down nearly 4% over two sessions, with the 'AI doom' narrative — driven by token optimization and open-model competition from Chinese rivals — weighing on the group. UBS characterizes the AI trade as 'maturing, not breaking,' but the near-term pressure on software names is visible.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz escalation: strait effectively closed; commodities surge
bullets.body: A shipping insider reports nothing is transiting the Strait of Hormuz despite US assurances, and Iran's top negotiator Qalibaf stated the strait situation 'will not return to pre-war conditions.' Trump threatened to bomb an Iranian bridge or power plant for each ship attacked in the strait. Since the Iran war began, commodity prices have surged: sulfur +142%, European natural gas +97%, jet fuel +44%, WTI crude +30%, wheat +18%.

bullets.title: Oil rallies to six-week highs; crude inventory build surprises to upside
bullets.body: Oil prices hit six-week highs on Trump's Iran threats and US production declines, though EIA data showed a surprise crude inventory build of +2.01M barrels vs. the consensus draw of -879K. Cushing inventories, however, drew down 674K barrels vs. a prior build of +430K, supporting the broader oil price narrative.

bullets.title: NVDA surges 2.9% intraday; Jensen Huang pushes back on 'efficiency kills demand' narrative
bullets.body: NVDA jumped 2.9% to a session high, with options flow showing the most bullish positioning of any name. CEO Jensen Huang argued 'everyone's got it backwards' on the Kimi K3 efficiency story, saying better AI models drive more compute demand. Separately, the White House accused Chinese AI startup MoonShot of illegally obtaining banned NVIDIA Blackwell chips via Thailand to build the Kimi K3 model.

bullets.title: NVIDIA targeting 1,000 Vera racks/day; shifting Vera Rubin pitch to token economics
bullets.body: NVIDIA is aiming to produce up to 1,000 Vera racks per day after already shipping hundreds of thousands of Grace standalone servers. The company is simultaneously shifting its Vera Rubin pitch toward token economics and scaling Texas assembly operations, cementing its push for AI CPU dominance alongside GPU leadership.

bullets.title: Early Q2 earnings season beats running strong: 83% EPS, 84% sales, 11% guidance raises
bullets.body: With fewer than 100 S&P 500 companies having reported, 83% beat EPS estimates, 84% beat sales estimates, and 11% raised forward guidance vs. only 3% lowering — a robust early-season read-through for the market.

bullets.title: Market breadth divergence at historic extreme: 6 of 9 rallying sectors had negative internals
bullets.body: Only 13 days since 1990 have seen six or more sectors simultaneously show price-vs-breadth daily divergences. Yesterday, 6 of 9 sectors that rallied showed negative breadth, meaning the index gains are concentrated in a small number of large-cap names rather than broad participation — a potential warning signal.

bullets.title: Margin debt hits past-market-top levels; Goldman high-beta basket surges
bullets.body: Margin debt has reached levels seen at prior market peaks, with one source characterizing conditions as 'very bearish looking.' At the same time, Goldman's high-beta momentum basket posted its biggest one-day surge since March 2021, highlighting the bifurcated risk posture in the market.

bullets.title: Gold hits $4,155/oz (+2%); silver surges 8.7% past $60/oz
bullets.body: Spot gold extended gains to $4,155.87/oz (+2%) and silver broke above $60/oz, up 8.7% over the past 72 hours. The moves reflect geopolitical risk premium (Iran-Hormuz), real yield anxiety, and dollar weakness dynamics all converging simultaneously.

bullets.title: China rare earth curbs: IEA warns $6.5T in global production at risk, market pricing in zero
bullets.body: The IEA estimates China's rare earth export restrictions could jeopardize $6.5 trillion in annual production outside China, with the US and Europe bearing nearly half the impact. Commentators note the market appears to be pricing in virtually zero risk from these supply constraints — a significant disconnect.

bullets.title: Cloud compute shortage to drive AMZN/MSFT/GOOGL price increases; margin expansion likely underestimated
bullets.body: With compute heavily constrained by AI demand, AMZN, MSFT, and GOOGL are expected to raise cloud prices, potentially driving margin expansion that the market is not pricing in. One commentator argues the AI era could produce the opposite of the feared margin compression — a sustained pricing power cycle lasting years.

bullets.title: GOOGL earnings tonight; stock up 90%+ YTD with capex set to nearly triple
bullets.body: Alphabet reports after the close with the stock up over 90% year-over-year. Google's capex is on track to nearly triple in two years. Separately, Reddit is reportedly considering cutting off Google's access to its content for AI training purposes, a potential licensing flashpoint.

bullets.title: TSLA reports tonight with 5% expected move; Musk bull-posting on RoboTaxi
bullets.body: Tesla reports after the close with options implying a 5% move. The stock was trading below all major moving averages ahead of the print. Elon Musk is actively bull-posting on X about the RoboTaxi program, and previously described Optimus as 'the biggest product ever, not just for Tesla.'

bullets.title: Atlanta Fed survey: business inflation expectations ease to 2.2% in July
bullets.body: Year-ahead business inflation expectations fell to 2.2% in July from 2.3% in June per the Atlanta Fed's latest survey, continuing the gradual disinflation trend even as commodity prices are surging on Iran-related supply disruptions.

bullets.title: Senate Clarity Act crypto bill advances with no Democrat support; federal officials banned from issuing crypto
bullets.body: Senate Republicans released updated Clarity Act text with White House-backed ethics rules and are pushing for a vote next week. The updated bill includes a ban on presidents and federal officials from issuing or sponsoring cryptocurrency. No Democrats have endorsed the text, leaving bipartisan passage uncertain.

bullets.title: Data center developers seeking to sell majority equity stakes worth tens of billions
bullets.body: Major US data center developers are working with investment banks to sell controlling equity stakes, with combined deal value in the tens of billions of dollars and activity expected this summer. Separately, proposed legislation would require data centers to cover grid upgrade costs, a potential capex headwind for operators.

bullets.title: Chinese AI models gaining market share; smuggled Western chips now cost 2–2.5x premium
bullets.body: Chinese AI models are now being used more than US-made ones globally. The cost premium for smuggled Western hardware in China has risen from 1.3–1.7x to 2–2.5x through early 2026, driving Chinese labs toward domestically produced alternatives from Huawei and Cambricon on price grounds.
